transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I guess… I’m here because eating has started to feel really out of my control. Like, once I start, it’s not just normal eating anymore. It feels like I kind of disappear, or go on autopilot, and something else takes over. I’ll be thinking the whole time, like, “Stop, stop, you don’t want to do this,” but I just keep going anyway.

And it’s not even like I’m enjoying it exactly. It’s more like I can’t interrupt it once it’s happening. I keep eating until I feel like I can’t stand it anymore, physically and mentally. It’s scary because I’m there, I know what I’m doing, but I also feel like I’m not really in charge of it. That’s the main reason I came in.
Can you describe what happens after one of these episodes? Do you feel ashamed, guilty, or do you try to compensate for it in some way, like skipping meals or exercising more?

Yeah… I do. I mean, I feel awful after. It’s not just guilt, it’s like panic. Like the second I realize how much I ate, I get this feeling that I have to do something immediately, or it’s just going to sit there in me and turn into weight. I know that sounds… I don’t know, extreme, but in the moment it feels completely real and urgent.

So usually I end up going to a bathroom somewhere in the dorm, or if I’m on campus and I don’t want anyone to notice, sometimes a quiet floor of the library. I’ll wait until it seems empty, or I’ll try to be really careful about noise, and then I make myself throw up. It’s embarrassing to say that out loud. I don’t really plan it like, “This is what I’m going to do today,” but after I eat like that it feels almost automatic, like I can’t calm down until I’ve done it.

And afterward I don’t even feel good exactly. Maybe relieved for a little bit, but mostly ashamed and kind of disgusted with myself. Then I start worrying that someone heard me or that people can tell, so it becomes this whole cycle of hiding it and feeling worse.
How often do these episodes happen? And when you say you make yourself throw up, does that happen after most of these eating episodes, or only sometimes?

It’s… it’s not just sometimes. I wish I could say it was like, once in a while when I’m really stressed, but for most of this semester it’s been happening several times a week. The eating part and then the throwing up after — they kind of go together most of the time for me.

I’ve tried to think back and be honest about it, because part of me wants to make it sound less bad, but over the last few months I don’t think there’s really been a week where it fully stopped. Like, maybe the exact number changes week to week, but it’s not a rare thing. It’s been… regular. Too regular. And usually after one of those episodes, I end up making myself throw up because I feel like I can’t stand not doing it.
Besides making yourself vomit, do you ever try to compensate for the eating episodes in other ways, like fasting, severely restricting your food, or exercising excessively?

I’m not really sure how to answer that, honestly. The vomiting is the main thing I know I do after, like that’s the thing that feels most… immediate, I guess. Like I get this panic and that’s where my brain goes.

With the other stuff, I don’t know. I don’t want to say yes if I’m not sure what counts as “severely” restricting or “excessively” exercising. I mean, I definitely think about food a lot after, and I’ll tell myself I should “be careful” or “make up for it,” but I don’t know if that’s the same as what you’re asking. Sometimes I probably avoid eating normally because I feel gross or scared, but it’s hard for me to separate what’s intentional from just feeling too anxious or ashamed to deal with food.

Exercise-wise… I wouldn’t say that’s the main way I compensate, not compared to throwing up. I guess I’ve had thoughts like I should go run it off or something, but I don’t really know that I have a clear pattern there. The vomiting is the part I’m more sure about.

Outside of making yourself vomit, do you ever go without eating for long periods, eat very small amounts of food, or push yourself to exercise a lot more than you think you should in order to make up for the eating episodes?

I don’t really know. I mean… not in a clear, organized way, I guess. The throwing up is the part I’m sure about because it’s so direct — like I eat, I panic, and then I feel like I have to do that.

With not eating, sometimes after it happens I’ll tell myself, “Okay, tomorrow I’m barely going to eat,” or I’ll think I should just avoid food because I already messed up. But then I don’t know if that counts as going without eating for a long time, because it’s not like I have a specific rule I always follow. It’s more like I feel too disgusted or anxious to eat normally, and I kind of pick at things or put off eating, but I’m not sure how much of that is me compensating versus just feeling awful.

And with exercise… I’ve had the thought that I should work it off, but I don’t think that’s really the main thing I do. I don’t want to overstate it and make it sound like I’m doing these intense workouts all the time to cancel it out, because I’m not sure that’s true. The thing I know happens is the vomiting. The rest is more messy in my head, like thoughts and intentions and sometimes avoiding food, but I don’t know if it’s a pattern the way you’re asking.

latest_inference.note: The patient's pattern of recurrent eating episodes followed by self-induced vomiting and other compensatory behaviors aligns with the diagnostic criteria for bulimia nervosa (F50.2). The absence of regular anorectic behaviors such as prolonged fasting, severe food restriction, or excessive exercise, and the prominence of purging following binge-like eating, make F50.0 (anorexia nervosa) less likely.
